## Challenge

We need to...

::: {style="margin: 1em;"}
1. define the costs and benefits of each strategy and
2. explain why individuals would choose one strategy over another. 
:::

::: {.fragment .fade-in}
To that end, we will develop a [**formal equilibrium model**]{.underline},
:::

::: {.fragment .fade-in}
i.e., we will apply [**neoclassical orthodoxy**]{.underline}. [\[cue Wilhelm scream\]]{.text-mono .text-muted}
:::

## Economy

We assume an agrarian subsistence economy in which...

::: {style="margin: 1em;"}

1. there is no trade or migration (the economy is isolated),
2. production occurs on farms privately held by households, and
3. factors are limited to labor (a variable input) and land (a fixed input).

:::

## Production

The energetic output of an individual farm is given by...

::: {.r-stack}
![](figures/production-0-axes.svg)

![](figures/production-1-total.svg){.fragment .fade-out fragment-index=1}

![](figures/production-3-marginal.svg){.fragment .fade-in-then-out fragment-index=2}
:::

## Utility

We assign to each farm a time budget, $T$, and assume that they are utility
maximizers:

::: {style="margin: 2em 1em;"}

|            |                                                               |
|------------|---------------------------------------------------------------|
| Clients:   | $\max U_{c} = f(T-L) + wL \quad\;\; \text{s.t.}\;\; L \leq T$ |
| Patrons:   | $\max U_{p} = f(T+L) - wL$                                    |
: {.eq-table}

:::

where $w$ is the market wage and $L$ is time invested in wage-labor.

::: {.fragment .fade-in .min-callout-note style="margin-top: 2em"}
{{< iconify pixel:lightbulb >}} [note:]{.title} When $L = 0$, production reduces 
to pure subsistence, $f(T)$, in which case, there are no patrons or clients.
:::

| Clients:   | $\max U_{c} = f(T-L) + wL \quad\;\; \text{s.t.}\;\; L \leq T$ |
